feasibility_reasoning: The core mechanism works. Custom properties inherit, and the data-wt~= gate stops an unset var() from overriding as unset under !important. [data-wt~=t][data-w-id][data-w-id] keeps the (0,3,0) prefix. The per-widget <style> comes before each div (ChromeWidgetView.tsx:391-392), so an inner widget wins by source order today and also by nearest-ancestor var resolution, as long as var names are per template token. The faithful what-if transform reproduces the target DOM: 32 blocks become 16 templates, 31 elements get data-wt, 2 colour-only blocks remain. What decides against the change as written is device handling. The 'device' value is the renderer container width (ResizeObserver, BuilderRenderer.tsx:250-279, deviceForWidth :208) or an explicit prop (MobileDrawerBody.tsx:33 device="mobile", PatternPicker.tsx:199, EventPreviewCanvas.tsx:629, WordPressPreviewDialog.tsx:171), and SSR is deliberately desktop-first (BuilderRenderer.tsx:236-242). 'Static @media' therefore breaks parity in popups (PopupHost.tsx:240), narrow content columns (ContentRenderer.tsx:78), the 768-1023 px mobile drawer, admin previews and the pre-hydration first paint. The vars must be keyed off [data-builder-renderer][data-device] (BuilderRenderer.tsx:293); nested renderers with different devices remain unsolved.
blocking_issues: Device selection via viewport @media contradicts the container-width / explicit-prop device model (BuilderRenderer.tsx:208,250-279,293; MobileDrawerBody.tsx:33). It must switch vars by [data-builder-renderer][data-device], or visual parity fails in popups, narrow columns, the drawer at 768-1023 px, admin previews and the pre-hydration mobile paint.

Var names must be per template token, not shared per property. Today A's generic rule (0,8,1) beats nested B's title fallback (0,6,1) for h1-h6 (typographyCss.ts:114,155), and a shared --wt-fs would let B's value win through inheritance.

Invalid authored values change behaviour. A parse-time invalid declaration falls back to the theme rule today, but through var() it becomes unset/inherit. cleanCssValue only strips {};<> (typographyCss.ts:44-53), so a whitelist like the slider's cssLen (sliderVariants.tsx:860-868) is needed.
The template must be unlayered and placed at the end of the public CSS. Inside a Tailwind @layer, layered !important beats unlayered !important and the cascade flips.

Scope and tests are missing from the file list. String-shape tests: typographyMapping.test.tsx:114-247, AuthorByline.cascade.test.tsx, chromeWidgetViewParity, widgetFrameOwnership, typographyMinFontSize, liveTypography, sliderTypographyFidelity. Cross-tab live typography uses BroadcastChannel plus a head <style> (liveTypography.ts:39-56). joinUsSizeCss (8-attribute specificity, :50,68) and slider instanceCss (class x3 + viewport @media, sliderVariants.tsx:870-890) are separate systems worth about 1 block; drop them.
The verification claim of zero '<style>[data-w-id=' blocks is false. hover, overrideCss and scopedCss stay coalesced in the same block (ChromeWidgetView.tsx:247-283,308), and prod keeps 2.

The H6 benefit is overstated. Only 2 of 102 responsive font sizes in prod state differ by device, and the data-device flip plus 25 grid-column mutations still trigger the 797-element recalc. HW-2 also conflicts with hydration H10(b) on the same CSS in the same file.
effect_reasoning: Bytes. On prod HTML (gzip-9), removing the rules and adding data-wt plus vars gives -58 KB raw / -5.1 KB gz with the template moved to CSS, or -4.1 KB gz with it inline. Fixture brotli-5 nets only -1.05 KB (44.6 -> 43.6 KB) because br already removes the repetition. The document is not the long pole (HWF-5: FCP/LCP flat for -25..32 KB gz). The template adds about +0.85 KB gz to the render-blocking CSS, which is the long pole: about +4-5 ms FCP/LCP mobile at 5-6 ms/KB. Attribution. 'TBT 158->25' is P0->P3, which also includes HW-3/4/5/6; HW-2 was never isolated. The existing isolations show nothing: fixture no-JS C_notypo vs B gives TBT 74/157 -> 131/168; P1->P2 gives 23-116 -> 0-133. With-JS what-if (this review: fixture, h2, interleaved, faithful template transform, B doc 344 vs 391 KB). Batch 1 (3+3): FCP +0.00 s, LCP +0.15 s, TBT -76 ms, score -3. Batch 2 (4+4): FCP 0, LCP -0.06 s, TBT +41 ms, score 0. Pooled TBT medians are A ≈267 ms and B ≈333 ms. Style&Layout medians are 890 vs 725 ms with overlapping ranges. Desktop: delta 0. All of this sits inside the A/A noise (TBT ±464 ms). Mechanism. Parse and style tasks sit before FCP today (sim FCP 4.06 s fixture, 3.1 s PSI), so TBT does not count them. The only in-window channel is the post-hydration whole-document recalcs (3 x 31-37 ms observed, 110 ms latent per LA 4b). About 450 -> 50 universal-bucket :is() selectors could trim each recalc by about 10-20 %, i.e. -10..-25 ms TBT mobile at x4. Cheaper alternatives: SC-7 (serve brotli) gets most of the transfer saving with no code change, and a ChromeWidgetView-only version with data-device-keyed vars keeps the style-node benefit.
